research_rationale: Executive Order 13900 of December 17, 2019 (84 FR 69983, Federal Register issue of December 20, 2019) closed executive departments and agencies and excused their employees from duty on Tuesday, December 24, 2019, the day before Christmas Day, with agency-head discretion to keep offices open, treatment of that day under Executive Order 11582 and 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 6103(b) for pay and leave, an OPM implementation direction, and general provisions. Every provision is confined to or tied to December 24, 2019, so each was exhausted by its own terms when that day ended. The end is recorded as December 24, 2019 inclusive; the exclusive reading (ending when the day begins) is the alternative. No held instrument revokes, extends or amends the order. The working text is the official Federal Register page text (machine-extracted from the PDF), not an authenticated transcription. The dossier's note that the target provision in Executive Order 11582 is not located is not an ending: section 3 only cites that 1971 order, which cannot revoke a later one.
savings_reason: Employees' excused absence on December 24, 2019, and the pay and leave treatment of that day, accrued on that day. They are surviving effects of the executed closure, not continuing commands of Executive Order 13900; the order has no savings clause and the held searches show no later instrument touching it.

research_rationale: Executive Order 8341 of February 8, 1940 (5 FR 643, Federal Register issue of February 10, 1940) is a one-paragraph order whose only operative act is to revoke Executive Order No. 8323 of January 22, 1940, which had abolished Customs Collection District No. 43 (Tennessee), revoked the designations of Memphis, Chattanooga and Nashville as customs ports of entry, and extended the limits of District No. 42 (Kentucky) and District No. 45 (St. Louis). The held text says the earlier order "is hereby revoked." The act has no deferred effective date, condition, report or continuing duty, so it was performed and exhausted when signed on February 8, 1940. No instrument held in the repository revokes, amends or extends Executive Order 8341, so no earlier or later end displaces that date. The working text is the official Federal Register page text (machine-extracted from the PDF, OCR), not an authenticated transcription; the page number and date were read from it.
savings_reason: The revocation of Executive Order No. 8323 was executed on February 8, 1940. That consequence accrued on execution; it is a surviving effect, not a continuing command of Executive Order 8341. The order has no savings clause and the held searches show no later instrument touching it.
